summary: A platform-owned process actor is a strong architecture for durable agent work if it is the sole transition authority and every external effect is fenced, evidenced, and recoverable.

points.text: The actor must own canonical state and compare-and-set transitions. Model outputs, worker logs, callbacks, and chat messages are untrusted proposals until the actor validates attempt ID, current state, schema, and policy.
A leased claim needs an attempt or fencing token checked by every commit and effect gateway. Expiry without fencing permits a delayed worker to act after replacement work has started.

Typed verdicts should distinguish completed, rejected, failed, cancelled, timed out, needs-input, and needs-approval, each with permitted successors and required evidence. Boolean success erases operationally important meaning.
Budgets, timers, retries, approvals, compensation, and terminal evidence belong to process policy. Leaving them inside a model loop makes recovery nondeterministic and state difficult to audit.
